issues.detail: The Greek 'χουζα' (Chuza) is a proper name, but the Vietnamese translates it as 'Chu-xa'. More importantly, the phrase 'επιτροπου ηρωδου' means 'steward of Herod', but the Vietnamese 'quản gia của Hê-rốt' misses the possessive relationship correctly if interpreted as a title; however, the main issue is the mistranslation of 'αιτινες' (wealthy/rich) as 'của cải' (possessions/wealth). The Greek describes the women as 'rich' (adjective), while the Vietnamese says they serve 'from their wealth' (prepositional phrase).

The Greek 'απο των υπαρχοντων αυταις' means 'from what they possessed/had'. The Vietnamese 'từ của cải của họ' changes the nature of the possession from a general state of having to specific 'wealth/assets'.
